name: Tomahawk River
gaugeName: TOMAHAWK R nr McCORD, at OUTLET of WILLOW RES, WI
blurb: Tomahawk River in Wisconsin between Wisconsin DNR-listed public accesses.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.notes: A lake-chain paddle from Tomahawk Thoroughfare to WVIC’s Minocqua Dam Recreation Area. The existing take-out area marker is below the dam: land at the signed upstream access and use the portage rather than paddling toward it. WVIC lists a 75-foot carry; inspect current access and the carry during your shuttle. Lake winds and boat traffic matter; this is not a free-drifting river-time estimate.
sections.routeReview: Minocqua Dam requires a land carry to reach the downstream access area. WVIC lists a canoe portage. Access markers are available, but no continuous dotted paddling line crosses the dam.

notices.title: Minocqua Dam: portage required
notices.text: The marked access area is downstream of the dam. WVIC documents a canoe carry around it; do not paddle through the dam. Check the signed landing, carry and parking before launching. Exact portage geometry is not shown.

putInAccess.operator: Town of Minocqua (ownership 'Town' in the WDNR record)
putInAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — public boat access inventory
putInAccess.note: Agency-listed access area; the marker does not identify the exact water-edge landing. Confirm the signed approach and current access conditions with the site manager. DNR notes that non-DNR sites in this inventory are not actively maintained.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed public approach to Tomahawk Thoroughfare Access. The map shows the access area; find the designated landing on arrival and check current site conditions.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: WVIC — Minocqua Dam Recreation Area, site 9
takeOutAccess.note: WVIC’s current recreation page links its 2021 map identifying site 9 and a canoe portage. Its detailed site inventory describes a 75-foot carry and a separate tailwater access. Imagery places the retained DNR point downstream of the dam. The point remains an approximate facility area; no precise portage geometry or bank side is assigned.
takeOutAccess.directions: Reach WVIC’s Minocqua Dam Recreation Area from Dam Road. The existing Area marker is at the downstream access. When arriving from the Minocqua lake chain, use the signed landing and portage around the dam; do not paddle across the dam to reach the marker. Inspect both ends of the carry during your shuttle and confirm current conditions with WVIC.

sections.notes: A long river-and-flowage trip from the downstream Minocqua access through Cedar Falls and Willow Flowage. Carry around Cedar Falls and Willow Dam. The listed take-out area is farther downstream on Willow Dam Road. Both markers are approximate; inspect signed access and both carries before launching. The 31.9-mile planning value is preliminary. Allow for lake winds, carries and possible overnight stops.
sections.routeReview: Cedar Falls and Willow Dam require land carries. WVIC lists canoe portages at Cedar Falls Campground and Willow Dam Recreation Area. No exact portage geometry or continuous dotted line through these barriers is approved.

notices.title: Cedar Falls and Willow Dam: portages required
notices.text: DNR advises all paddlers to carry around Cedar Falls. WVIC lists canoe portages at Cedar Falls Campground and Willow Dam Recreation Area. Use signed carries; do not paddle through the falls or dam. Confirm current access and any campground fees before launching.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin Valley Improvement Company — Willow recreation map, sites 1 and 3

notices.title: Willow Flowage: check low-water access
notices.text: DNR reports seasonal low water affecting some landings and campsites. Check its conditions page before choosing access or overnight stops. The Willow Dam Road marker is an approximate access area; inspect the signed landing during your shuttle.

When arriving from the Minocqua lake chain, use the signed landing and portage around the dam; do not paddle across the dam to reach the marker. takeOutAccess.operator: Wisconsin DNR (WDNR record lists no manager)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Willow Flowage canoe access and public landing inventory
takeOutAccess.note: DNR confirms a public carry-in below Willow Dam. Its landing inventory and separate GPS handout place this facility about 807 metres apart; the handout coordinate is beside the road in imagery. Retain the inventory coordinate as an approximate river-access area, not a verified shoreline or parking pin. The exact approach remains unresolved; no straight connector is mapped.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed canoe access on Willow Dam Road; DNR lists its road address as 4716 Willow Dam Road, Hazelhurst. The Area marker uses DNR’s landing inventory and does not pinpoint the footpath or shoreline. Find the signed landing during your shuttle.

sections.takeOut: Lower Tomahawk River Pines Sna Canoe Landing
sections.difficulty: Class II at Echo Falls (DNR recommends portaging)
sections.notes: From the Willow Dam Road canoe access to the Lower Tomahawk River Pines access area. Echo Falls lies on this reach; DNR strongly recommends carrying around its Class II rapids. The take-out is above Prairie Rapids, which is a separate downstream hazard. Both markers are approximate facility areas. The 14.5-mile planning distance is preliminary; inspect the signed landings and carry before launching.
sections.routeReview: Echo Falls requires a separate carry review before any continuous course is drawn. Exact landings and the carry are not mapped; DNR recommends portaging its Class II rapids.

notices.title: Echo Falls: portage recommended
notices.text: DNR strongly recommends a carry around Echo Falls, a Class II rapid downstream of Highway Y. The listed take-out is upstream of Prairie Rapids; do not continue into that separate Class II reach without a new trip plan. Exact carry and shoreline connections are not shown.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Tomahawk River paddling guidance
